title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 7 vs. Denver Broncos
headline: Cardinals' offense stalled again in a Week 7 home loss to Denver; LaFleur took blame for red-zone calls, backed Jacoby Brissett, and singled out Trey McBride and Michael Wilson as the players who will turn it around.
summary: LaFleur said Denver's explosive plays hurt Arizona, starting with Bo Nix scrambling against man coverage after rush lanes opened. He took responsibility for the goal-line failure, calling the sack a bad call and saying he got greedy by passing after a quarterback sneak from the half-yard line. He also owned the decision to kick a field goal on fourth-and-goal from the two at 6-3, saying he expected a low-scoring game. He declined to single out Jacoby Brissett, framing the offensive struggles as collective, and said Brissett was hit often because Denver took away the underneath throws and Arizona had to go over the top. He praised Michael Wilson for drawing a lot of pass interference penalties and called Trey McBride and Wilson "studs" who will be big reasons the offense turns around. On the dropped end-zone pass by Bam Knight, he said he trusts Knight to make that play at some point. He was non-committal on right tackle Hayden Conner, saying there was good and bad and the pass pressure on Brissett needs film review. He stressed penalties, red-zone execution and playing better at home as the correctable issues.

signals.claim: McBride will be a central part of the offense's turnaround
signals.note: The coach publicly named McBride as a core piece, which supports a steady target share even while the offense struggles.
signals.quote: They're studs. They're awesome. Like they're going to be huge reasons why this thing flips.

signals.claim: Wilson will keep drawing pass interference penalties and remains a featured downfield target
signals.note: He is creating plays through penalties that don't show up in the box score, but he is clearly a focal point of the passing game.
signals.quote: Mike drew a bunch of pies again today.

signals.claim: Brissett remains the starting quarterback; LaFleur did not directly confirm this when asked and deflected blame from him
signals.note: He was sacked 10 or 11 times and the offense is struggling, so the starting job and his fantasy floor deserve watching.
signals.quote: I'm not even going to talk about any of the individuals.

signals.claim: Knight will get another chance to make a catch in the red zone
signals.note: He dropped a catch in the end zone but keeps the coach's confidence, so red-zone involvement is likely to continue.

signals.claim: Conner's performance will be judged on film; no commitment either way
signals.note: Pass protection problems persist, which hurts Brissett and the passing-game ceiling.
signals.quote: I thought there was some good stuff, but obviously there were some times

topics.detail: LaFleur called the sack on the goal-line series a stupid call, said he got greedy by passing after the sneak, and listed penalties, a holding on a draw play and a stalled progression as other problems. He called it all correctable.

He kicked a field goal on fourth-and-goal from the two at 6-3 and also chose to kick on another fourth-down situation, saying both were in-the-moment decisions based on an expected low-scoring game. He said other weeks might be different.
Denver took away the short throws, which forced Arizona to go downfield and hold the ball longer. That led to heavy pressure and the sacks on Brissett.
Denver's big plays, including a long Bo Nix scramble against man coverage, hurt the defense. LaFleur wants to review the defensive tape before saying more.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Post-game Press Conference | Week 7 | Falcons vs. 49ers
headline: Falcons beat the 49ers behind a +4 turnover margin. Penix (3 TD passes) got a clear vote of trust, Drake London was praised as a hard-yards chain mover, and Kendal Daniels returned a week after a hospital stay.
summary: Stefanski was proud of the team's effort in beating a very good 49ers team. He said the +4 turnover margin was where the win started, and he called the fast, physical play the team's identity. Kendal Daniels got a game ball for playing and calling the defense a week after being in the hospital. Stefanski said he trended toward playing early in the week and had a good week of practice. Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes against an excellent defense that doesn't give up big plays, and Stefanski said the staff trusts him despite his limited number of starts. Pressure on Penix was low, and Stefanski spread the credit among the line, the receivers, the quarterback and OC Tommy's game plan. He said the four trusted tight ends mean personnel groupings will vary game to game, and he praised Nick Muse's goal-line touchdown. He called Maason Smith's first half dominant and praised Drake London's blocking and hard yards in the run and pass game. He also singled out Jessie Bates III for a great interception and a late play. The win was the team's first at home this season.

injuries.detail: Was in the hospital a week earlier. He was evaluated Monday, his symptoms were treated, he felt better through the week, practiced well, and played and called the defense.

signals.claim: Daniels has recovered enough to play a full game after last week's hospital stay.
signals.note: He played, so he's healthy for IDP purposes.
signals.quote: he kept feeling better and better throughout the week

signals.claim: Daniels wears the green dot and calls the defense.
signals.note: The play-caller role points to a high-snap, every-down role for IDP managers.

signals.claim: Penix remains the trusted starting quarterback.
signals.note: He threw three TDs against a tough defense and faced pressure on only 6 of 35 dropbacks, so his QB2 value is steady.
signals.quote: We trust Mike.

signals.claim: London will keep working as a chain mover on hard yards in both the run and pass games.
signals.note: His physical role, including blocking and over-the-middle work, points to steady target volume.
signals.quote: hard yards in the run game, hard yards in the pass game.

signals.claim: Tight end usage and personnel groupings will vary week to week, with four tight ends trusted.
signals.note: Muse scored on a well-designed goal-line play, but the split among four tight ends makes his usage hard to predict.
signals.quote: it'll be game to game in terms of what we lean into

signals.note: Smith dominated the first half with pass-rush pressure, which is a good sign for IDP value.
signals.quote: he's just winning and he's winning quickly and harassing the offensive line

signals.note: Bates made an interception and a late play, and the coach says he is playing at a high level, which is good for IDP managers.
signals.quote: he's playing at a high level.

topics.detail: Atlanta finished +4 in turnover margin and Stefanski said the team played fast and physical, which he called the identity the team wants.
Stefanski said the plan was to be quick early because the 49ers rush well and tackle very well. He credited Tommy and the offensive staff for the game plan and for the creativity of the offense.

The Falcons erased an early 14-3 deficit and scored 26 unanswered points. Stefanski highlighted the middle eight, with a field goal at the end of the first half followed by a touchdown after the break.
Stefanski credited the whole offense for low pressure on Penix, citing protection, receivers getting open, quick decisions and the game plan rather than the offensive line alone.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Loss to Bengals
headline: Lamar Jackson's availability for next week is unresolved (to be sorted out over the next couple of days) and the Ravens' run game remains a concern after a 35-13 loss to the Bengals.
summary: Minter called the 35-13 loss to Cincinnati a tale of two halves. Baltimore started well but failed to take advantage of its first-half opportunities, then lost momentum and let the game snowball in the second half. He said the team is too much of a momentum team and needs to be more even keel. He blamed the defense for missed tackles, short throws turning into big yards after the catch, and explosive plays, calling it a bad second-half effort that starts with him. On offense he said he is certainly concerned about the inefficient run game over the last few weeks, that the team is searching for better answers, and that it is trying to build continuity on the offensive line. He admitted the offense has been a tale of two halves for a couple of games and needs better forward-thinking adjustments. Asked about a serious injury (the question was garbled and referred to 'Vegas'), he had no update. On whether Lamar Jackson could practice and play next week, he said the team will figure it out over the next couple of days.

injuries.detail: Coach said the team will figure out over the next couple of days whether Jackson can practice and play next week; no definitive status given.

signals.claim: Jackson's ability to practice and play in Week 8 will be determined over the next couple of days.
signals.note: Jackson's status for Week 8 is undecided, so monitor practice reports before setting lineups and consider a backup QB plan.
signals.quote: over the next couple days we'll figure that out.

signals.claim: The run game has been inefficient and the staff is searching for answers to sustain drives.
signals.note: Henry's rushing production is at risk while the run game struggles and the line lacks continuity, though no individual was named.
signals.quote: we got to search for those better answers

topics.detail: Minter said he is concerned about the run game's inefficiency over recent weeks and is trying to create continuity on the offensive line with what the team has available.
The offense has been a tale of two halves for a couple of games; Minter wants forward-thinking adjustments and a stronger second-half plan.
Missed tackles on short throws turned into yards after the catch and explosive plays, and Bengals receivers made them pay. Minter called it a bad second-half effort to be reviewed on tape.
Minter said the team is too momentum-driven and needs consistency and an even-keel mindset. He said the team has control over it and the tough conversations will continue.

title: Dave Canales speaks after Sunday’s game against Buccaneers
headline: Taylor Moton (fibula fracture, ankle/knee involvement) will miss substantial time, and Carolina's offense looked shaky after a 22-point turnover disaster; Bryce Young took the brunt with pressure and two INTs.
summary: Canales was clearly disappointed after a loss to Tampa Bay that he blamed mostly on turnovers: a sack-fumble returned for a touchdown, two interceptions, a dropped punt, and a blocked kick that led to 22 points for the Bucs. He credited Tampa Bay's run game plan, but said Carolina missed tackles, failed to fit gaps, and didn't contain the backs in space. He said the offensive line had trouble with stunts and movement up front, and that Tampa Bay generated pressure on Young like no one had this season. He said he liked his defensive calls and that the issue was execution, not play-calling. Canales said the run game was efficient and should have produced more points, but the turnovers killed focus and momentum. He said Taylor Moton suffered a fibula fracture with ankle and knee involvement and will be out a substantial amount of time, though he wouldn't say if it is season-ending until all the workup is done. Young was described as positive, encouraging and ready to move on, though he did not have a good day. With a short week, Canales said the team had a quick Monday-style meeting to move on.

injuries.detail: Rolled up on during the game; fibula fracture, with ankle and knee involvement. Out for a substantial amount of time; season-ending status not yet confirmed pending full workup.

signals.claim: Moton will miss a substantial amount of time with a fibula fracture.
signals.note: Losing the starting right tackle hurts an offensive line that already struggled against pressure, which affects the outlook for Young and the run game.
signals.quote: it's going to be a substantial amount of time

signals.claim: Young is ready to move on and bounce back after a rough turnover-filled game under heavy pressure.
signals.note: Young faced pressure unlike any seen this season and threw two interceptions, so his outlook depends on whether the line can fix its issues, especially without Moton.
signals.quote: He's ready to move on from this one and get back to good football.

topics.detail: The sack-fumble, two interceptions, dropped punt and blocked kick led to 22 Tampa points. Canales said he had never been part of a half like it.
Tampa Bay ran effectively with varied styles (gun, under center, zone, gap). Canales cited missed tackles and gap-fit errors, but defended the play calls.
Stunts and movement up front gave the line trouble, and Canales said Tampa Bay's pressure on Young was unlike anything the team had seen this season. He said opponents may try to copy it.
Canales said the run game was efficient throughout the day and should have produced more points had the turnovers not put Carolina in a hole.
Carolina plays again on Thursday, so the team has little time to review and recover. Canales said the week of practice felt good and he is trying to figure out how it led to this result.

title: Zac Taylor Speaks Following Week 7 Victory In Baltimore | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals rallied from 13-0 to win 35-13 in Baltimore, with Ja'Marr Chase (148 yards, all in the second half) and the pass game leading the way; Eric (knee) and Doug (quad) are injury watches, and Bryan Cook returned.
summary: Taylor said the Bengals struggled on third down on both sides of the ball in the first half and trailed 13-0. They then scored five straight touchdowns in the second half while the defense got five straight stops. He said the offense put itself in second-and-ten situations early and faced heavy third-down pressure. In response, the team chose to throw more and found its 'bread and butter' pass game rhythm. He praised the backs and linemen for a steady run game, noting there was no 15-yard run but that wasn't needed. Ja'Marr Chase had no first-half catches but produced all 148 yards after halftime, and Taylor called him 'so valuable' and praised his halftime leadership. Drew Sample's trick-play touchdown and a missed tackle by Samaje Perine on a touchdown run were highlighted. On defense, Taylor singled out the edge rushers, saying Boye Mafe had two sacks, Cashius Howell got his first, and Dexter Lawrence finished one. On injuries, he mentioned a knee for 'Eric' and a quad for 'Doug' and said they would see how those develop, and that Bryan Cook came back. The team now turns to Tennessee, and Taylor stressed it is just one win in 17 games.

injuries.detail: Taylor mentioned 'Eric' with a knee injury; the name is likely a transcription of Erick All, but this is not certain. He said they would see where it ends up.
Taylor said Cook came back in this game.
Taylor said 'Doug' had a quad injury and they would see where it ends up. The player cannot be matched confidently to the roster.

signals.claim: Chase remains a central, high-value target in the passing game and was productive after a quiet first half.
signals.note: Chase had 148 yards, all in the second half, and Taylor lauded his value and leadership, supporting a strong WR1 outlook.
signals.quote: He's so valuable. He's such a big target.

signals.claim: Mafe is an effective edge rusher who affects the passer.
signals.note: His two-sack game, praised by Taylor, helps his IDP value.
signals.quote: Awesome. You know it just affects the passer. He got the two sacks

signals.note: Recorded his first career sack as part of the pass rush effort, which is worth watching for IDP managers.
Scored on a trick-play touchdown that the team had repped for years; this is likely a one-off rather than a usage change.
Taylor highlighted Perine's missed-tackle touchdown run as a big moment, which hints at red zone involvement.

signals.claim: His knee injury status will be evaluated in the coming days.
signals.note: If 'Eric' refers to Erick All, his availability for Tennessee is in question, which could affect the TE room.
signals.quote: Eric was a knee.

topics.detail: The Bengals were stuck in second-and-ten and third-and-long situations early. They decided to lean on the passing game rather than run more, and the backs and linemen still contributed enough to stay on schedule.

The defense struggled on third down in the first half but held Baltimore to field goals on key drives. Taylor praised the pass rush and coverage while acknowledging Lamar Jackson's creativity and explosive plays are inevitable against Baltimore.
Taylor said the win reaffirms the team's potential but is just one win. He wants a strong week of practice before facing Tennessee.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Titans: October 25th, 2026
headline: Browns beat Tennessee 27-24 as the run game improved and Quinshon Judkins returned. KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. are set to keep getting the ball in space.
summary: Monken called the win a gutsy team effort that was far from perfect. Cleveland fell behind 10-0 and then 14-0 for the second week in a row and has to fix its slow starts. The team turned the ball over a couple of times, but he said it ran the ball better, was better on first and third down, and scored on all of its red-zone chances. He called Deshaun Watson's performance the most complete game of the seven so far, close to the Pittsburgh game in composure and control, with the one exception of the slant turnover. Monken said that on that play the quarterback has to trust that Denzel Boston has a break and a cross-face option. He praised KC Concepcion as a diligent, humble, competitive player who is hard to bring down and protects the ball, and said Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. need to keep getting touches in space. He said he did not plan for any particular player to get targets. Two two-minute drives and a rhythm built on a working run game spread the touches around. He said the run game benefited from facing a four-down front, since that is what Cleveland sees in practice, unlike the odd-front teams it had recently faced. He also said Watson's legs and a mix of under-center and gun looks are still being worked on. The team now turns to Pittsburgh.

injuries.detail: Monken cited 'getting Quinshon back' as a reason the run game and offensive continuity improved.

signals.claim: Watson is trending up and played his most complete game of the season, and the offense will keep using his legs and a mix of under-center and gun.
signals.note: Monken's praise for his composure and late-game play supports confidence in Watson's weekly floor, though the slow starts and turnover remain concerns.
signals.quote: He has something in him to be able to make plays when it counts.

signals.claim: Concepcion will keep getting the ball in space, including some touches running the ball, in addition to his targets.
signals.note: Monken called him a weapon who is hard to bring down, and the team plans to keep finding him touches.
signals.quote: He is a weapon. We've got to continue.

signals.claim: Fannin will continue to be featured, with the team trying to get him the ball in space.
signals.note: He was grouped with Concepcion and Judkins as hard-to-tackle players the offense wants to feed.
signals.quote: Same with Harold right.

signals.claim: Judkins is back in the lineup and helped the run game improve.
signals.note: His return gives Cleveland a better rushing attack and a boost to his fantasy value.
signals.quote: obviously getting Quinshon back.

signals.note: Boston was cut off on the slant that became a turnover, and Monken put some of the responsibility on the quarterback to trust the break.
signals.quote: He's got a break face. He's got a cross face.

topics.detail: Cleveland fell behind 10-0 and 14-0 for the second week in a row and has to start faster.
Monken said the run game improved against a four-down front, which resembles what the offense sees in practice, compared with the odd-front teams of recent weeks.
Cleveland turned the ball over a couple of times but scored on all of its red-zone chances and was better on first and third down.
Cleveland gave up a lot of rushing yards and three touchdowns to Tennessee's lead back. Monken credited the opponent and said he needs to watch the tape before drawing conclusions.

title: Campbell on Week 7 performance
headline: Lions beat Green Bay behind a strong defense and Jared Goff. Amon-Ra St. Brown is in a groove, and Khalil Dorsey should see more defensive snaps.
summary: Campbell called the win over a hot Packers team a good division win, with the defense as the big story. The secondary played sticky, challenged throws, and held up deep, and the front was disruptive. He singled out Khalil Dorsey for stepping in with big plays and said D.J. Wonnum's block on a field goal cost the team nothing. On offense he said the team played well until two turnovers (two fumbles) and a failed fourth-down try, which he called frustrating. He said he trusted his decision to go for it on his own 24 in a tied game because he believed they'd convert and knew the defense would get the ball back if they didn't. He praised Jared Goff as playing at a very high level and said the offensive line protected him well. He said Amon-Ra St. Brown is reliable and that the team wants to get him the ball in space to cut loose. A player returning from a long injury, whom he called "Beebe", made a huge play. Campbell said he is healthy and only rusty, and that he was managed through the first half. DeAndre Carter was praised on special teams, and the game ended with the ball going to Jahmyr Gibbs with one second left. Next up is Minnesota.

injuries.detail: Campbell didn't use a full name. He said the player, called "Beebe", played his first game back from a major injury and is healthy with just rust. He was managed through the first half, and Campbell said he'll keep improving with each rep. The name match is inferred, so treat it with caution.

signals.claim: Detroit will keep looking to get St. Brown the ball in space so he can run after the catch.
signals.note: Campbell called him reliable and said they want to let him cut loose, which points to continued strong target quality and big-play upside.
signals.quote: he's reliable. You can count on it.

signals.claim: Goff will continue to run the offense with full trust from the coaching staff, including in late-game situations.
signals.note: Campbell has complete confidence in Goff, and the line is protecting him well, which supports his passing output.
signals.quote: He's just going to take care of the football.

signals.claim: Dorsey will get more defensive snaps going forward after his two big plays.
signals.note: He is mainly an IDP or deep-league consideration, but his defensive role is growing from a small base.
signals.quote: there's no reason why he wouldn't get a few more plays

signals.claim: He is healthy and will keep improving as he gets more game reps after his return.
signals.note: For IDP leagues, a safety who made a big play in his first game back and was only held back by rust is worth rostering. The name match is inferred from Campbell calling him "Beebe".
signals.quote: he's going to get better and better

topics.detail: Campbell went for it on his own 24 in a tied game and the Lions didn't convert. He said he believed they would get it and knew the defense could get the ball back if not.
He called the two fumbles enormous and said the team was fortunate the defense recovered. He said they cost Detroit a chance to extend the lead.
He praised the front, the backers, and the back end for playing sticky and disruptive and challenging throws downfield. He said confidence and trust are building and the team is getting better.
He praised DeAndre Carter's contribution on the cover units. He also praised D.J. Wonnum's block of a field goal.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts at Vikings postgame
headline: Colts leaned on a run-heavy plan with JT and Seth McGowan sharing the bulk of the carries; Steichen is staying with Daniel Jones, and a Jones injury question is still open after the 16-10 loss.
summary: Steichen said the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings came down to a few missed plays, and he praised his team's fight. The plan was to run the ball and establish the run, because Minnesota was expected to blitz heavily. Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan got the bulk of the carries, and Steichen felt the run game was good. The passing game was not where he wanted it. He pointed to heavy pressure, quick throws, running backs staying in to block in max protection, and a double-move shot where Daniel Jones got hit. He defended his defense, calling it phenomenal, citing a fourth-and-one stop on the opening drive and several third-down stops. He also backed kicker Spencer Shrader (the 'Spence' he refers to), who missed kicks, including a 56-yard attempt and one to tie the game. Steichen said he has not considered a quarterback change, and Jones threw a late interception. Asked about quarterback injuries, he said he would gather more information from the doctors. He opened by noting injuries to Walley and Cam Taylor-Britt, with no details. He dismissed a question about job security and said he is focused on the next game.

injuries.detail: Steichen listed him among the injuries to start the press conference, with no details.
Also named among the injuries to start the press conference, with no details.
Asked about quarterback injuries, Steichen said he would gather more information from the doctors. The question was ambiguous, so this may not refer to Jones.

signals.claim: Taylor got the bulk of the carries in a run-first plan, and the run game will remain a strength.
signals.note: Taylor is the primary rusher in a plan built on establishing the run, which supports his volume.
signals.quote: JT and Seth got a bulk of the carries.

signals.claim: McGowan shared the bulk of the carries with Taylor and ran hard.
signals.note: McGowan has a real role in the run plan, though it is unclear how much he'd keep if the game script changes.
signals.quote: I thought Seth ran hard.

signals.claim: Jones remains the starting quarterback and Steichen has not considered a change.
signals.note: Jones's job looks safe for now, but the passing game struggled and Steichen could not yet say whether he is injured.

topics.detail: The Colts planned to run the ball and keep throws quick against Minnesota's heavy blitz. Running backs also had to block in max protection, so the outlets were limited.
Steichen called the defense phenomenal. He cited a fourth-and-one stop on the opening drive, multiple third-down stops, and holding Minnesota to a field goal on the last drive.
Steichen has a ton of confidence in kicker Spencer Shrader after missed kicks, including a 56-yard attempt and one to tie the game. He called it an off day.
The Vikings showed multiple looks and switched up their pressure. Steichen credited Harrison Smith for a great play on a cover-four coverage.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Oct 25 | Postgame Press Conference
headline: Malik Willis had his best game as a starter, and Ollie Gordon's physical, gap-scheme run game is the identity Hafley wants to build around.
summary: Hafley was pleased with the 28-25 win over the Jets, the team's first of the year and first in the division. He praised the offensive line, said Bobby called a great game, and called Malik Willis's performance his best. He went for a fourth-and-one late after consulting the offensive line, and the conversion sealed the game. Hafley said Willis was decisive, got the ball out quickly, took care of it and ran when he could. He also said Ollie Gordon ran hard and that a physical back who can close out games fits the team's gap-scheme, run-heavy identity. He was critical of the defense, citing missed assignments in man coverage, several 50-50 balls and a Jets offense that played physically up front. He said the team is still learning how to take a lead and keep it, and admitted he could have made a better call on a late fourth-down situation. Zayne Anderson was described as a backup who made a big play when called on.

signals.claim: Willis is playing with growing decisiveness and quicker decisions, and the offense can lean on him as the starter.
signals.note: Hafley called it Willis's best game, citing quick releases, good decisions and ball security. He also noted Willis is effectively a rookie starter with only six games of work, so more growth is expected.
signals.quote: I thought he got rid of the ball quick. I thought he made good decisions.

signals.claim: Gordon will keep working as the physical back in a gap-scheme, direct-run offense, closing out games with the lead.
signals.note: Hafley praised how hard he ran and said the offense wants a physical back who wears defenses down. That points to a solid workload, especially when Miami is ahead.
signals.quote: physical back that can close out games and wear people down as you go

signals.claim: Anderson is a backup who rotates in when needed, after starting the year as a rotational starter.
signals.note: He made a big play near the goal line but remains a depth player, so he has little fantasy or IDP value unless injuries hit ahead of him.
signals.quote: his role right now is to be a backup.

topics.detail: Hafley consulted the offensive line before going for it on fourth-and-one, liked what he saw in their eyes, and trusted them. The conversion sealed the win, and he credited the line for a strong day in the run game and in protection.

Hafley said there were many uncharacteristic missed assignments, especially in man coverage. A running back broke free on the first drive, and several 50-50 balls went the Jets' way. He credited the Jets' offense and their physical front, and said the tape needs a hard look.

topics.topic: Learning to win and play with a lead
topics.detail: This was the first time Miami took an early lead and kept it. Hafley highlighted a goal-line defensive stand, a pressure by Simpson that forced a bad field goal, and the late runs that closed the game. He admitted he could have made a better call in a late fourth-down situation.

Hafley wants the team built on toughness and physicality, starting with the offensive line and with receivers and tight ends who run hard after the catch. He called this the first division game and said that physical identity needs to be the standard.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Advancing to 6-0, Harrison Smith’s Interception & Blake Cashman’s Sacks
headline: Vikings are 6-0, but the offense is still inconsistent, especially the run game. Aaron Jones had his knee checked, Jordan Addison cleared a concussion check, and Kyler Murray's legs are becoming a real weapon.
summary: O'Connell was pleased with the win coming off the bye, crediting the crowd, special teams (which won field position by 5-6 yards), and a turnover-free game. He felt the offense left a lot out there despite nine explosive plays, citing inefficient runs, late penalties, a false start, and a few missed third-and-long throws. He said the team is 'not far off' and is confident it will get going. He wanted to run the ball better, and took responsibility for the failed third- and fourth-and-short calls early on. He praised Kyler Murray's third-down run as a read of the defense that opened up a big play for Jordan, and noted Murray has made big plays with his legs and arm in 2-3 straight games, including a touchdown to T.J. Hockenson. A Murray-to-Jordan play was called back late, though his comments suggest it was Addison. On injuries, Myles Price had a stinger but returned, Aaron Jones had the same knee evaluated, and Jordan Addison was cleared after a concussion check. Blake Cashman earned another game ball for his play-calling, blitzing and pass breakups, and Harrison Smith's game-closing interception (No. 40) was highlighted.

injuries.detail: Suffered a stinger but was evaluated and returned to the game.
Had the same knee evaluated during the game; O'Connell said the team came out 'relatively clean' and gave no further update.
Pulled aside for a quick concussion evaluation and cleared to return.

signals.claim: Murray's designed and read-based runs will keep being part of the offense, and defenses must account for his legs on third downs.
signals.note: Rushing upside gives Murray a higher fantasy floor and ceiling, with his legs forcing defenses to adjust.
signals.quote: Kyler recognized it and took off and had a chance to score.

signals.claim: Cashman will continue as the defense's green-dot signal caller and a key blitzer.
signals.note: He is a high-impact IDP linebacker with a green-dot role and blitz usage.
signals.quote: He's just flying all over the place.

signals.note: Jefferson was targeted on a missed third-and-long play and had a big gain early in the second half; O'Connell expects more production as the offense stacks plays.
signals.quote: Justin's screaming through the defense right there.

signals.claim: Addison was cleared for the concussion evaluation and returned to the game.
signals.note: A good sign for his availability, but concussion checks warrant monitoring this week.
signals.quote: he was cleared to return.

signals.note: The knee was evaluated, which could affect his run-game workload if it lingers.

title: Kellen Moore recaps Saints' loss to Steelers in Paris | Saints-Steelers Postgame | 2026 NFL Week 7
headline: Saints run game was a disaster in the Paris loss (17 carries for 18 yards) and everything is being re-evaluated in the bye week. Tyler Shough got praise, and CJ Donaldson and Justin Reid are in concussion protocol.
summary: Kellen Moore said the Saints lost a game of small margins to the Steelers, who made a few more plays on third downs and in the red zone. He kept coming back to the run game: 17 carries for 18 yards, which included a couple of Tyler Shough scrambles. He called that unacceptable and said it forced New Orleans to throw more than it wanted. He gave no specific fixes. The plan is to use the bye week to 'evaluate everything' from the start of the season and not jump to conclusions. He also said the team has to stop the Steelers' run game, which kept them in manageable third downs, and that tackling will be reviewed on film. He said the kicker, who has missed a kick or extra point in six of seven games, will be evaluated during the bye. Shough was praised for battling and keeping the Saints in position to have chances late. On health, Moore said two players are in concussion protocol, CJ (Donaldson) and Justin Reid, and that everything else should be fine. He gave no update beyond 'we'll see' on a player the reporter called 'Jordan Tyson', who is still in the recovery process with no practices during the bye.

injuries.detail: Moore said he had a concussion-related issue in the game. No timeline was given.
Moore said he had a concussion-related issue in the game. No timeline was given. The bye week helps his recovery time.

The reporter's name, 'Jordan Tyson', is not on the provided roster, so this is the likely intended player. Moore said there are no practice times during the bye, he is in the training room and 'building back up', and the team will see coming out of the bye whether he is activated.

signals.note: Moore praised Shough's performance and said his scrambles padded a run game that totaled 18 yards. The offense may lean on his arm and legs until the ground game is fixed.

The staff will work through the bye, with some personal time for people. Moore said the team has to carry forward the positives from a good week of practice in Paris and from the win in New York the week before.

title: Coach John Harbaugh: 'That was a players' win in every way'
headline: J.J. McCarthy started and played well in a win over Houston, Devin Singletary scored the OT winner after weeks as a healthy scratch, and the Giants lost Tremaine Edmunds and Jermaine Eluemunor.
summary: Harbaugh called the Week 7 overtime win over the Texans a players' win. He praised the team's response after last week's criticism of the defense and its fourth-quarter conditioning. He said new starting QB J.J. McCarthy ran the offense seamlessly, with no procedural penalties, clock problems or formation issues, and made throws. He said McCarthy has scars from his past but has grown stronger, and that Jameis Winston still helped prepare him and talked to the team before the game. Harbaugh credited Cam Skattebo and the offensive line for the late run game and credited Devin Singletary for the winning touchdown after being the odd man out for weeks. On defense he singled out Deonte Banks, who covered Houston's top receiver tightly, Micah McFadden, who made several tackles including a key one on a sweep, and Abdul Carter, who he said took over the game as a pass rusher and against the run. He acknowledged injuries to Tremaine Edmunds and Jermaine Eluemunor, with Eluemunor headed for surgery. He said the team will focus on Philadelphia and a quick turnaround after the bye, which he called the two most important games of the season. He also said he is not worried about the young kicker, Zavada, who needs to hit the ball straight.

injuries.detail: Described by a reporter as lost this week, and Harbaugh did not dispute it. No diagnosis or timeline was given.
He tried to keep playing against doctors' advice. He is now having surgery and will travel with the team once he is allowed.

Harbaugh said the team's resilience 'maybe started with Jackson' when he went down. This is likely Dart, but no status or timeline was given.

He described the team's mental toughness as built from stacked adversity, including injuries, and said the Giants have been the stronger team late in games all year.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (10/25) | Week 7
headline: Garrett Wilson saw only three targets and Aaron Glenn took the blame, saying getting him the ball is in the game plan; T'Vondre Sweat left with a knee injury.
summary: Aaron Glenn was highly disappointed after the Week 7 loss that dropped the Jets to 2-5, and he put the blame on himself. He said the defense played poorly in the first half, allowing 21 points on 3-4 drives, with leaky yardage against the run and the opposing QB making plays with his arms and legs. He called the slow start puzzling but said the team was ready to play and that the defense improved in the second half. He pointed to no takeaways, poor third-down defense and red-zone struggles as problem areas. He admitted he should have used his timeouts late in the first half, expecting a red-zone stop. On Garrett Wilson's three targets, he said that is on him, that getting Wilson the ball is in the game plan, and that he will work with the offensive play-caller to fix it. T'Vondre Sweat has a knee injury, but Glenn gave no further detail. He defended the program's direction despite the record and the fan frustration, citing the team's resilience.

injuries.detail: Left the game with a knee injury; Glenn gave no further detail on the extent or availability.

signals.claim: The Jets will make a concerted effort to increase Garrett Wilson's targets in upcoming games.
signals.note: Glenn took blame for Wilson's three targets and promised changes, so a bounce-back in volume is plausible, though the offense's quality is still a concern.
signals.quote: we have to do everything we can to try to get him the ball

signals.note: A knee injury with no clear timeline matters for IDP managers and for the run defense's depth.
signals.quote: he has a knee

topics.detail: Glenn was puzzled by the first-half run defense, with the opponent falling forward for extra yards. He said the defense improved in the second half but lacked takeaways, third-down stops and red-zone execution.
Glenn said he should have used his timeouts late in the first half when the opponent was in the red zone, since he believed the defense would get a stop.
At 2-5, Glenn insisted the team is on the right track, citing the players' effort and improvement, and acknowledged fan frustration.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Saints
headline: Steelers leaned on a Jaylen Warren/Rico Dowdle backfield duo in a 16-10 win over the Saints in Paris, hitting a 30-rush goal; Rodgers showed mobility and the Browns are up next.
summary: McCarthy was upbeat after the 16-10 win in Paris, calling it a special trip and a good road test for his team. He said the game looked like training camp, with Jalen Warren and Rico Dowdle getting the bulk of the work, and he was pleased the team reached its goal of 30 rush attempts. He said the team wanted to own the line of scrimmage on both sides and hit that target, and he noted the young offensive line is piling up consecutive starts. He admitted that going 1-for-4 in the red zone is not where they want to be, but said it is good to win and still have things to fix. He praised a big defensive play that took points off the board, and said the defense is getting more comfortable with scheme adjustments each week. He also praised a scramble-type play by the quarterback, saying he can still move. He said the team was better on third downs by staying in manageable distances and running the ball. Next up is a divisional game at home against the Browns, who beat them earlier, and McCarthy called it a rivalry game.

signals.note: A run-focused plan with a clear two-back split supports both backs' touch floors, though it caps either one's ceiling.

signals.note: He is named alongside Warren as part of a featured duo, and the team wants 30 rushes a game.

signals.note: Occasional rushing upside adds a small boost to his fantasy floor.

They went 1-for-4 in the red zone, which McCarthy called unsatisfactory. Third-down offense improved thanks to manageable distances and the ability to run in those situations.
A big defensive play took points off the board, and the defense is growing more comfortable with scheme adjustments each week.
The short week and the overtime game the week before shaped their rest and sleep plan, and the Paris trip will influence the plan for the Browns game.

title: Kyle Shanahan Breaks Down Loss to the Falcons
headline: 49ers lost to Atlanta on four turnovers; WR Jordan Watkins keeps rising, and Christian McCaffrey's thigh looked fine but is unconfirmed until Shanahan sees the tape.
summary: Shanahan called the loss 'too sloppy to win.' The 49ers turned the ball over four times and forced none, and penalties kept Atlanta's drives alive. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions. On the second, a defender dropped out of a blitz that San Francisco didn't see, and Shanahan said Purdy has to throw it away. Kittle and 'KB' (Kaelon Black) each lost a fumble. He called the first fumble, in the red zone with the 49ers up 14-3, the turning point. An offside penalty on fourth down then gave Atlanta a free first down, and Atlanta got 10 points without the 49ers touching the ball. He praised the wideouts, especially Watkins, who has played well for three weeks and made a number of big plays. He also liked the run game but said it couldn't stay with it late because of the score. McCaffrey hurt his thigh and returned, and Shanahan said he looked all right but wants to check the tape. He didn't know the plan at kicker after the team's workouts and hasn't discussed it yet.

title: Todd Bowles on Division Win in Carolina: Full-Team Effort | Press Conference
headline: Bucs ran for 49 carries in a dominant division win over Carolina, leaning on a three-man RB group (Gainwell, Tucker, Irving) while Baker Mayfield threw just 11 passes in his return from a thumb injury; Diaby had a 3-sack day.
summary: Bowles called the win a full-team effort, saying the plan was to control time of possession against an explosive Carolina offense, and the Bucs cashed in with touchdowns instead of field goals. The offensive line and running backs dominated, with 49 runs, which made the day easy for Baker Mayfield, who returned from injury and threw only 11 passes. Bowles said they hadn't specifically planned to protect Mayfield's thumb, but the run game was gaining 4-5 yards a carry so they stuck with it. He said all three backs, Kenny Gainwell, Sean Tucker and Bucky Irving, had good runs, and he wants the ground game to become an identity but stressed it needs consistency. The defense produced three takeaways, with the D-line getting off the ball and coverage and rush complementing each other, so they didn't need to blitz much. Bowles said the breakout games from Yaya Diaby (three sacks) and Elijah Roberts (scoop and score) were coming, as the pass rush finally got results. Special teams were critical, with a turnover on a punt return and strong kickoff coverage. He noted the defense slacked off late with backups in, and said the team needs the same attitude next week; it was the first of six division games.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans lost to the Browns after blowing a 14-0 lead. Saleh blamed the defense (run D, tackling, pass rush) and said Cam Ward missed throws but it's "not a quarterback problem."
summary: Saleh was blunt after the loss to Cleveland. He said the defense wasn't good enough in any phase: run defense, tackling, coverage, pass rush and coaching. The Browns' late touchdown drive and field goal drive came largely on the ground and on checkdowns that went for more yards than they should have. He said the offense started fast with two scoring drives, but the team should have "boat raced" Cleveland in the first half. The turning point was failing to score from first and second and goal at the one-yard line. After a fourth-and-goal stop and a takeaway, the Browns scored to make it 14-14. Asked whether the team has a quarterback problem, he said no and called it a problem across the board. He said Ward missed some throws he has to make, including one to Bellinger late, but also made an excellent throw to Elic Ayomanor under pressure to tie the game. He did not question the goal-line execution and credited Cleveland for battling inside the five. The team had a chance in the final two-minute drive and didn't make the play.

signals.note: Saleh defended Ward and rejected the 'quarterback problem' framing, but admitted he missed throws he should make, so his consistency is still a concern.
signals.quote: He missed some throws that he's got to make.

signals.note: Ayomanor was the target on Ward's best throw of the day, a touchdown-tying completion under pressure, which suggests he's a trusted option in big moments.
signals.quote: he made up for it with an unbelievable throw to elec while getting hit

signals.note: Ward missed a throw to Bellinger late in the game, which shows he was a target in a key moment but the connection failed.
signals.quote: he missed the throw on belly there at the end

topics.detail: Saleh called the run defense uncharacteristically poor. He said the team missed or broke many tackles and was slow getting to checkdowns, which let Cleveland extend late drives.

Saleh said the pass rush, the pressure designs and the coverage were all not good enough. Cleveland's quarterback had taken 24 sacks over the first six weeks, and Tennessee failed to pressure him with a lead.

The offense failed to score from first and second and goal at the one-yard line, then lost momentum when a takeaway was followed by a Browns touchdown. Saleh said they have to be able to push it in from there, and he didn't think the second-and-one sneak call was reversible.
After scoring on the opening two drives, the offense went a couple of quarters without points. Saleh called the game 'grimy' and said the team should have blown Cleveland out in the first half.
